drivingQuestion: What is Rabbi Eliezer's scriptural source for holding that the priests do not take a consecrated ancestral field at the Jubilee until another person has redeemed it — and does an owner who redeems it during the second Jubilee cycle count as that 'another'?
outcomeNote: Rava settles the first question — R' Eliezer derives his ruling from ״בצאתו״, only a field leaving another's possession. The second question is answered by Rav Ashi in each version, but the איכא דאמרי preserves the opposite baraita and the opposite ruling, so the unit closes with two rival versions rather than one decision.

segments.he: אָמַר רַבָּה: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר? אָמַר קְרָא: ״וְאִם לֹא יִגְאַל אֶת הַשָּׂדֶה לֹא יִגָּאֵל עוֹד, וְאִם מָכַר אֶת הַשָּׂדֶה וְהָיָה הַשָּׂדֶה בְּצֵאתוֹ בַיּוֹבֵל״.
segments.en: «Rabba said: What is the reason for Rabbi Eliezer’s» opinion? It is because the «verse states:» “And if he will not redeem the field, or if he sold the field to another man, it shall not be redeemed anymore. But the field, when it goes out in the Jubilee, shall be holy for the Lord, as a dedicated field; his ancestral possession shall be for the priest” (Leviticus 27:20–21). According to Rabba, Rabbi Eliezer maintains that these verses teach two separate halakhot, and should be read as follows: «“And if he will not redeem the field…it shall not be redeemed anymore,”» as an ancestral field, and: «“Or if he sold the field…But the field, when it goes out in the Jubilee…»his ancestral possession shall be for the priest.” Accordingly, if the field has not yet been sold to another man, it is not transferred to the priests during the Jubilee.

segments.he: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: סַכִּינָא חֲרִיפָא מַפְסְקָא קְרָאֵי? אֶלָּא אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר כִּדְתַנְיָא: ״לֹא יִגָּאֵל״ — יָכוֹל לֹא תְּהֵא נִגְאֶלֶת שֶׁתְּהֵא לְפָנָיו כִּשְׂדֵה מִקְנָה? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר ״עוֹד״ — לִכְמוֹת שֶׁהָיְתָה אֵינָהּ נִגְאֶלֶת, אֲבָל נִגְאֶלֶת שֶׁתְּהֵא לְפָנָיו כִּשְׂדֵה מִקְנָה.
segments.en: «Abaye said:» Does «a sharp knife cut» through the «verses,» that they may be interpreted by reading the words out of order? «Rather, Abaye said: The reason for Rabbi Eliezer’s» opinion is «as it is taught» in a baraita: Since the verse states: “And if he will not redeem the field, or if he sold the field to another man, «it shall not be redeemed,”» one «might» have thought that this means «it shall not be redeemed» at all by its owner, even «for it to be» treated «for him like a purchased field,» which remains in his possession until the Jubilee. Therefore, «the verse states: “Anymore,”» indicating that «it shall not be redeemed» in order for it «to» return to «the way it was,» i.e., to regain the status of an ancestral field, «but it» may be «redeemed for it to be» treated «for him like a purchased field.»

segments.he: אֵימַת? אִילֵּימָא בְּיוֹבֵל רִאשׁוֹן — אַמַּאי אֵינָהּ נִגְאֶלֶת? שְׂדֵה אֲחוּזָּה נָמֵי הָוְיָא! אֶלָּא פְּשִׁיטָא בְּיוֹבֵל שֵׁנִי.
segments.en: Abaye continues: According to this baraita, of «when,» i.e., about which time period, is the verse speaking? «If we say» that it is referring to a redemption occurring «during the first Jubilee» cycle in which the field was consecrated, then «why may it not be redeemed» in order for it to return to the way it was? At that point, «it is even» redeemable as «an ancestral field,» because if the owner redeems it then, it is not removed from his possession during the Jubilee Year. «Rather,» it is «obvious» that the baraita interprets the verse as referring to a redemption occurring «during the second Jubilee» cycle.

segments.he: וּלְמַאן? אִילֵימָא לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן, לְכֹהֲנִים נָפְקָא! אֶלָּא לָאו רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר, וּשְׁמַע מִינַּהּ טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר מֵהָכָא.
segments.en: «And according to whose» opinion is this baraita? «If we say» that it is «according to» either «Rabbi Yehuda or Rabbi Shimon,» this cannot be correct, as according to them, the field «leaves» the possession of the Temple treasury and is given «to the priests» during the first Jubilee Year, after which it may no longer be redeemed. «Rather, is it not» in accordance with the opinion of «Rabbi Eliezer,» who maintains that the field remains in the possession of the Temple treasury until it is redeemed, even during a subsequent Jubilee cycle? «And» consequently, «conclude from» this baraita that «the reason for Rabbi Eliezer’s» opinion is «from here,» i.e., from the superfluous term “anymore.”

segments.he: וְתִסְבְּרָא, רַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן הַאי ״עוֹד״ מַאי דָּרְשִׁי בֵּיהּ? אֶלָּא, הָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן — בְּשָׂדֶה שֶׁיָּצְאָה לַכֹּהֲנִים, וְהִקְדִּישָׁהּ כֹּהֵן, וְאָתוּ בְּעָלִים לְמִיפְרְקַהּ.
segments.en: The Gemara asks: «And can you understand» the baraita this way? If so, then «what do Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Shimon derive from this» term: «“Anymore”? Rather,» the baraita can be understood in accordance with their opinions as well, and «what are we dealing with here?» We are dealing «with» an ancestral «field» whose owner consecrated it and did not redeem it, «which left» the possession of the Temple treasury and was given «to the priests» during the first Jubilee Year; «and» the «priest» who received the field then «consecrated it, and» then the original «owner came to redeem it» from the Temple treasury.

segments.he: סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ אָמֵינָא: לָא תִּיפְרוֹק, שֶׁתְּהֵא לְפָנָיו כִּשְׂדֵה מִקְנָה — תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״עוֹד״, לִכְמוֹת שֶׁהָיְתָה אֵינָהּ נִגְאֶלֶת, אֲבָל נִגְאֶלֶת שֶׁתְּהֵא לְפָנָיו כִּשְׂדֵה מִקְנָה.
segments.en: It might «enter your mind to say:» Since the owner failed to redeem this field during the first Jubilee cycle, «it shall not be redeemed» by him at all, even «for it to be» treated «for him like a purchased field.» Therefore, «the verse states: “Anymore,”» indicating that «it shall not be redeemed» in order for it «to» return to «the way it was,» i.e., an ancestral field, «but it» may be «redeemed for it to be» treated «for him like a purchased field,» which remains in his possession only until the Jubilee Year.

segments.he: וְהָתַנְיָא: ״בִּשְׁנַת הַיּוֹבֵל יָשׁוּב הַשָּׂדֶה לַאֲשֶׁר קָנָהוּ מֵאִתּוֹ״, יָכוֹל יַחְזוֹר לַגִּזְבָּר שֶׁלְּקָחוֹ מִמֶּנּוּ? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״לַאֲשֶׁר לוֹ אֲחֻזַּת הָאָרֶץ״.
segments.en: «And» similarly, «it is taught» in a baraita: With regard to one who consecrated a purchased field and redeemed it, since the verse states: «“In the Jubilee Year the field shall return to the one from whom it was bought”» (Leviticus 27:24), one «might» have thought that the field «shall return to the» Temple «treasurer, from whom he bought it» when he redeemed it. Therefore, «the verse states» immediately afterward: «“To the one to whom the possession of the land belongs,”» i.e., it goes to the ancestral owner who initially sold the field to the one who consecrated it.

segments.he: יֵאָמֵר: ״לַאֲשֶׁר לוֹ אֲחֻזַּת הָאָרֶץ״, מָה תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר ״לַאֲשֶׁר קָנָהוּ מֵאִתּוֹ״? שָׂדֶה שֶׁיָּצָאת לַכֹּהֲנִים, וּמְכָרָהּ כֹּהֵן, וְהִקְדִּישָׁהּ לוֹקֵחַ, וּגְאָלָהּ אַחֵר — יָכוֹל תַּחְזוֹר לַבְּעָלִים הָרִאשׁוֹנִים? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״לַאֲשֶׁר קָנָהוּ״.
segments.en: The baraita continues: If so, «let» the verse simply «state: “To the one to whom the possession of the land belongs.” Why» must «the verse state» first: «“To the one from whom it was bought”?» The baraita answers: The verse is referring to an ancestral «field» whose owner consecrated it and did not redeem it, «which left» the possession of the Temple treasury and was given «to the priests» during the Jubilee Year, «and» the «priest» who received the field then «sold it» to another, «and» the «buyer» then «consecrated it, and another» person «redeemed it» from the Temple treasury. One «might» have thought that when the next Jubilee arrives, «it shall return to the original owner.» Therefore, «the verse states:» “In the Jubilee Year the field shall return «to the one» from whom «it was bought,”» indicating that the field is returned to the priest who sold the field.

segments.he: וְאִיצְטְרִיךְ ״לֹא יִגָּאֵל״, וְאִיצְטְרִיכָא לְמִיכְתַּב ״לַאֲשֶׁר קָנָהוּ״.
segments.en: The Gemara notes: «And» it «was necessary» for the Torah to write: «“It shall not be redeemed,” and» it «was» also «necessary» for it «to write: “To the one» from whom «it was bought,”» despite the fact both phrases apparently teach the same halakha, i.e., that after a consecrated ancestral field is left unredeemed and given to the priests during the Jubilee Year, it never returns to the original owner.

segments.he: דְּאִי כְּתַב רַחֲמָנָא ״לֹא יִגָּאֵל״, דְּלָא קָא הָדְרָה כְּלָל, אֲבָל הָכָא דְּקָא הָדְרָה, תִּיהְדַּר לְמָרַהּ קַמָּא, כְּתַב רַחֲמָנָא ״לַאֲשֶׁר קָנָהוּ״.
segments.en: The Gemara explains: «Because if the Merciful One had written» only: «“It shall not be redeemed,”» one might have thought that the field does not return to the original owner only in a case where the priest consecrates the field and the original owner redeems it, «as» an ancestral field that is consecrated by its owner and redeemed by another «does not return at all,» but is divided among the priests. «But here,» where the priest sold the field that he received and the field was consecrated by the buyer as a purchased field and subsequently redeemed by another, «as» the field «does return» to its owner in the Jubilee Year, perhaps «it should return to its original owner,» and not the priest. Therefore, «the Merciful One wrote: “To the one» from whom «it was bought,”» indicating that it returns to the priest.

segments.he: וְאִי כְּתַב רַחֲמָנָא ״לַאֲשֶׁר קָנָהוּ״, דְּלָא קָא יָהֲבִי בְּעָלִים דָּמֵי, אֲבָל הָכָא, דְּקָא יָהֲבִי דְּמֵי, תֵּיקוּם בִּידַיְיהוּ, כְּתַב רַחֲמָנָא ״לֹא יִגָּאֵל״.
segments.en: «And if the Merciful One had written» only: «“To the one» from whom «it was bought,”» one might have thought that the field does not return to its original owner during the Jubilee Year only in a case where the priest sold it and the buyer consecrated it, «as the owner did not give» any «payment for» the field to the Temple treasury. «But here,» where the priest consecrated the field and its original owner redeemed it, «as he gives payment for» the field to the Temple treasury, perhaps «it should remain in his hands» as his ancestral field. Therefore, «the Merciful One wrote: “It shall not be redeemed.”»

segments.he: וְאִי כְּתַב רַחֲמָנָא ״לֹא יִגָּאֵל״, וְלָא כְּתַב ״עוֹד״, הֲוָה אָמֵינָא: לָא תִּיפְרוֹק כְּלָל, כְּתַב רַחֲמָנָא ״עוֹד״, לִכְמוֹת שֶׁהָיְתָה אֵינָהּ נִגְאֶלֶת, אֲבָל נִגְאֶלֶת שֶׁתְּהֵא לְפָנָיו כִּשְׂדֵה מִקְנָה.
segments.en: «And if the Merciful One had written» only: «“It shall not be redeemed,” and did not write: “Anymore,” I would say» that «it shall not be redeemed at all,» as its original owner failed to redeem it during the first Jubilee cycle. Therefore, «the Merciful One writes: “Anymore,”» to indicate that «it shall not be redeemed» in order for it «to» return to «the way it was,» i.e., an ancestral field, «but it» may be «redeemed for it to be» treated «for him like a purchased field.»

segments.he: מַאי הָוֵי עֲלַהּ? אָמַר רָבָא, אָמַר קְרָא: ״וְהָיָה הַשָּׂדֶה בְּצֵאתוֹ בַיּוֹבֵל״, בְּצֵאתוֹ מִיַּד אַחֵר.
segments.en: The Gemara asks: «What» conclusion «was» reached «about it?» In other words, now that both suggestions have been rejected, what is the reason for Rabbi Eliezer’s opinion that a consecrated ancestral field that has not been redeemed by the Jubilee Year is not given to the priests? «Rava said» that the «verse states: “But the field, when it goes out in the Jubilee,» shall be holy for the Lord, as a dedicated field; his ancestral possession shall be for the priest” (Leviticus 27:21). The term “when it goes out” indicates that it is given to the priests only «when it goes out» during the Jubilee Year «from the possession of another» person, who redeemed it from the Temple treasury.

segments.he: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: בְּעָלִים בְּיוֹבֵל שֵׁנִי, כְּאַחֵר דָּמוּ אוֹ לָא?
segments.en: § «A dilemma was raised before» the Sages: According to Rabbi Eliezer, if the «owner» consecrated his ancestral field and failed to redeem it before the first Jubilee Year, but he redeemed it «during the second Jubilee» cycle, is he «considered like another» person who redeemed the field, in which case it is given to the priests at the following Jubilee Year, «or not,» i.e., as the one who ultimately redeemed the field first was the owner, does it remain in his possession as it would have if he had redeemed it during the first Jubilee cycle?

segments.he: תָּא שְׁמַע: ״לֹא יִגָּאֵל״ — יָכוֹל לֹא תְּהֵא נִגְאֶלֶת, שֶׁתְּהֵא לְפָנָיו כִּשְׂדֵה מִקְנָה? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר ״עוֹד״ — לִכְמוֹת שֶׁהָיְתָה אֵינָהּ נִגְאֶלֶת, אֲבָל נִגְאֶלֶת שֶׁתְּהֵא לְפָנָיו כִּשְׂדֵה מִקְנָה.
segments.en: The Gemara suggests: «Come» and «hear» a resolution of this dilemma from the following baraita: Since the verse states: “And if he will not redeem the field, or if he sold the field to another man, «it shall not be redeemed”» (Leviticus 27:20), one «might» have thought that this means «it shall not be redeemed» at all by its owner, even «for it to be» treated «for him like a purchased field.» Therefore, «the verse states: “Anymore,”» indicating that «it shall not be redeemed» in order for it «to» return to «the way it was,» i.e., an ancestral field, «but it» may be «redeemed for it to be» treated «for him like a purchased field.»

segments.he: אֵימַת? אִילֵּימָא בְּיוֹבֵל רִאשׁוֹן — אַמַּאי אֵינָהּ נִגְאֶלֶת? אֲחוּזָּה נָמֵי הָוְיָא! אֶלָּא פְּשִׁיטָא בְּיוֹבֵל שֵׁנִי.
segments.en: The Gemara continues: According to this baraita, of «when,» i.e., about which time period, is the verse speaking? «If we say» that it is referring to a redemption that occurs «during the first Jubilee» cycle, in which the field was consecrated, «why may it not be redeemed» in order for it to return to the way it was? At that point «it is even» redeemable as «an ancestral» field, since if the owner redeems it then, it is not removed from his possession during the Jubilee Year. «Rather,» it is «obvious» that the baraita interprets the verse as referring to a redemption occurring «during the second Jubilee» cycle.

segments.he: וּלְמַאן? אִי לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן — לְכֹהֲנִים נָפְקָא! אֶלָּא לָאו לְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר, וּשְׁמַע מִינַּהּ: בְּעָלִים בְּיוֹבֵל שֵׁנִי כְּאַחֵר דָּמוּ.

segments.he: וְתִסְבְּרַאּ?! רַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן הַאי ״עוֹד״ מַאי דָּרְשִׁי בֵּיהּ? אֶלָּא, הָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן? בְּשָׂדֶה שֶׁיָּצְאָה לַכֹּהֲנִים, וְהִקְדִּישָׁהּ כֹּהֵן, וַאֲתוֹ בְּעָלִים לְמִיפְרְקַהּ. סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ אָמֵינָא: לָא תִּיפְרוֹק, שֶׁתְּהֵא כִּשְׂדֵה מִקְנָה. תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״עוֹד״ — לִכְמוֹת שֶׁהָיְתָה אֵינָהּ נִגְאֶלֶת, אֲבָל נִגְאֶלֶת שֶׁתְּהֵא לְפָנָיו כִּשְׂדֵה מִקְנָה.
segments.en: The Gemara asks: «And can you understand» the baraita this way? If so, «what do Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Shimon derive from this» term: «“Anymore”? Rather, what are we dealing with here?» We are dealing «with» an ancestral «field» whose owner consecrated it and did not redeem it, «which left» the possession of the Temple treasury and was given «to the priests» at the first Jubilee Year; «and» the «priest» who received the field subsequently «consecrated it, and» then the original «owner came to redeem it» from the Temple treasury. It may «enter your mind to say:» Since the owner failed to redeem it during the first Jubilee cycle, «it shall not be redeemed» by him at all, even «for it to be» treated «for him like a purchased field.» Therefore, «the verse states: “Anymore,”» indicating that «it shall not be redeemed» in order for it «to» return to «the way it was,» i.e., an ancestral field, «but it» may be «redeemed for it to be» treated «for him like a purchased field.»

segments.he: וְהָתַנְיָא: ״יָשׁוּב הַשָּׂדֶה לַאֲשֶׁר קָנָהוּ מֵאִתּוֹ״, יָכוֹל יַחְזוֹר לַגִּזְבָּר שֶׁלְּקָחָהּ הֵימֶנּוּ? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״לַאֲשֶׁר לוֹ אֲחֻזַּת הָאָרֶץ״.
segments.en: «And» similarly, «it is taught» in a baraita: With regard to one who consecrated a purchased field and redeemed it, since the verse states: “In the Jubilee Year «the field shall return to the one from whom it was bought”» (Leviticus 27:24), one «might» have thought that the field «shall return to the» Temple «treasurer, from whom he bought it» when he redeemed it. Therefore, «the verse states: “To the one to whom the possession of the land belongs,”» i.e., the ancestral owner.

segments.he: מָה תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר ״לַאֲשֶׁר קָנָהוּ״? שָׂדֶה שֶׁיָּצְאָה לַכֹּהֲנִים, וּמְכָרָהּ כֹּהֵן, וְהִקְדִּישָׁהּ לוֹקֵחַ, וּגְאָלָהּ אַחֵר — יָכוֹל תַּחְזוֹר לַבְּעָלִים הָרִאשׁוֹנִים? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר ״לַאֲשֶׁר קָנָהוּ״.
segments.en: The baraita continues: If so, «why» must «the verse state: “To the one» from whom «it was bought”?» The baraita answers: The verse is referring to an ancestral «field that» was consecrated and not redeemed, and which therefore «left» the possession of the Temple treasury and was given «to the priests» at the Jubilee Year, «and» the «priest» who received the field then «sold it» to another, «and» the «buyer» then «consecrated it, and another» person «redeemed it» from the Temple treasury. One «might» have thought that when the next Jubilee arrives, «it shall return to the original owner.» Therefore, «the verse states:» “In the Jubilee Year the field shall return «to the one» from whom «it was bought,”» indicating that the field is returned to the priest who sold the field.

segments.he: וְאִיצְטְרִיךְ לְמִיכְתַּב ״לֹא יִגָּאֵל״, וְאִיצְטְרִיךְ לְמִיכְתַּב ״לַאֲשֶׁר קָנָהוּ״, דְּאִי כְּתַב רַחֲמָנָא ״לֹא יִגָּאֵל״ דְּלָא קָא הָדְרָא כְּלָל, כְּתַב רַחֲמָנָא ״לַאֲשֶׁר קָנָהוּ״.
segments.en: The Gemara notes: «And» it «was necessary» for the Torah «to write: “It shall not be redeemed,” and» it «was» also «necessary» for it «to write: “To the one» from whom «it was bought,” because if the Merciful One had written» merely: «“It shall not be redeemed,”» one might have thought that the field does not return to the original owner only in a case where the priest consecrates the field and the original owner redeems it, «as» an ancestral field that is consecrated by its owner and redeemed by another «does not return at all.» But in a case where the priest sold the field to another and the buyer consecrated it, perhaps it should return to its original owner. Therefore, «the Merciful One wrote: “To the one» from whom «it was bought,”» indicating that it returns to the priest.

segments.he: וְאִי כְּתַב רַחֲמָנָא ״לַאֲשֶׁר קָנָהוּ״, דְּלָא קָיָהֲבִי בְּעָלִים דְּמֵי, אֲבָל הָכָא, דְּיָהֲבִי בְּעָלִים דְּמֵי, דְּתֵיקוּם בִּידַיְהוּ, כְּתַב רַחֲמָנָא ״לֹא יִגָּאֵל״.
segments.en: «And if the Merciful One had written» merely: «“To the one» from whom «it was bought,”» one might think that the field does not return to its original owner at the Jubilee Year only in a case where the priest sold it and the buyer consecrated it, «as the owner did not give» any «payment for» the field to the Temple treasury. «But here,» where the priest consecrated the field and its original owner redeemed it, «as the owner gives payment for» the field to the Temple treasury, one might have thought «that it should remain in his hands,» as his ancestral field. Therefore, «the Merciful One wrote: “It shall not be redeemed.”»

segments.he: וְאִי כְּתַב רַחֲמָנָא ״לֹא יִגָּאֵל״, וְלָא כְּתַב ״עוֹד״, הֲוָה אָמֵינָא לָא תִּיפְרוֹק כְּלָל, כְּתַב רַחֲמָנָא ״עוֹד״, לִכְמוֹת שֶׁהָיְתָה אֵינָהּ נִגְאֶלֶת, אֲבָל נִגְאֶלֶת שֶׁתְּהֵא לְפָנָיו כִּשְׂדֵה מִקְנָה.
segments.en: «And if the Merciful One had written» only: «“It shall not be redeemed,” and did not write: “Anymore,” I would say» that «it shall not be redeemed at all,» as its original owner failed to redeem it during the first Jubilee cycle. Therefore, «the Merciful One writes: “Anymore,”» to indicate that «it shall not be redeemed» in order for it «to» return to «the way it was, but it» may be «redeemed for it to be» treated «for him like a purchased field.»

segments.he: מַאי הָוֵי עֲלַהּ? תָּא שְׁמַע: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: גְּאָלָהּ בְּעָלִים בְּיוֹבֵל שֵׁנִי — יוֹצְאָה לַכֹּהֲנִים בַּיּוֹבֵל.
segments.en: The Gemara asks: Since it has been established that the term “anymore” is necessary according to all opinions, «what» conclusion «was» reached «about» the original dilemma with regard to whether the owner is considered like another person during the second Jubilee cycle? The Gemara answers: «Come» and «hear» a proof from the following baraita: «Rabbi Eliezer says:» If the «owner redeemed it during the second Jubilee» cycle, it «leaves» the possession of the Temple treasury and is given «to the priests during the Jubilee» Year.

segments.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבִינָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי: הָאֲנַן לָא תְּנַן הָכִי, רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: אֵין הַכֹּהֲנִים נִכְנָסִין לְתוֹכָהּ עַד שֶׁיִּגְאָלֶנָּה אַחֵר! אֲמַר לֵיהּ: בְּעָלִים בְּיוֹבֵל שֵׁנִי כְּאַחֵר דָּמוּ.
segments.en: «Ravina said to Rav Ashi: But we did not learn this» interpretation of Rabbi Eliezer’s opinion in the mishna. Instead, the mishna states that «Rabbi Eliezer says: The priests» never «enter into» a consecrated field during the Jubilee Year «until another» person «redeems it» first. This indicates that if the owner, rather than any other person, is the one who ultimately redeems the field, it remains in his possession even if he did so during the second Jubilee cycle. Rav Ashi «said to» Ravina: «During the second Jubilee» cycle, the «owner» is «considered like another» person.

segments.he: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: גְּאָלָהּ בְּיוֹבֵל שֵׁנִי — אֵינָהּ יוֹצְאָה לַכֹּהֲנִים בַּיּוֹבֵל. אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבִינָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי: אַף אֲנַן נָמֵי תְּנֵינָא, רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: אֵין הַכֹּהֲנִים נִכְנָסִין לְתוֹכָהּ עַד שֶׁיִּגְאָלֶנָּה אַחֵר! אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אִי מִמַּתְנִיתִין הֲוָה אָמֵינָא: בְּעָלִים בְּיוֹבֵל שֵׁנִי כְּאַחֵר דָּמוּ, קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן.
segments.en: «Some say» a different version of the baraita and ensuing discussion: «Rabbi Eliezer says:» If the owner «redeemed it during the second Jubilee» cycle, it «does not leave» the possession of the Temple treasury and is not given «to the priests during the Jubilee» Year. «Ravina said to Rav Ashi:» Why must a proof be brought from this baraita? «We learn» in the mishna «as well» that «Rabbi Eliezer says: The priests» never «enter into» a consecrated field during the Jubilee Year «until another» person «redeems it» first. Rav Ashi «said to him: If» a proof is learned «from the mishna» alone «I would say» that «during the second Jubilee» cycle the «owner» is «considered like another» person. Therefore, the baraita «teaches us» that according to Rabbi Eliezer the owner is not considered like another person, and the field returns to him as an ancestral possession.

moves.cueHe: אָמַר רַבָּה: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר?
moves.summary: Rabba asks the scriptural basis of R' Eliezer's ruling in the mishna that the priests do not enter the field until another redeems it.
moves.about: the scriptural basis of R' Eliezer's ruling that the priests do not enter a consecrated ancestral field until another has redeemed it

moves.cueHe: אָמַר קְרָא: ״וְאִם לֹא יִגְאַל אֶת הַשָּׂדֶה לֹא יִגָּאֵל עוֹד״
moves.summary: Rabba answers by splitting Leviticus 27:20-21 into two independent derivations.
moves.about: brings the verse ואם לא יגאל את השדה לא יגאל עוד as the source of R' Eliezer's ruling

moves.cueHe: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: סַכִּינָא חֲרִיפָא מַפְסְקָא קְרָאֵי?
moves.summary: Abaye refutes Rabba's split reading: no sharp knife cuts verses apart.
moves.about: whether a verse may be cut apart and its clauses redistributed into two separate derivations

moves.cueHe: אֶלָּא אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר כִּדְתַנְיָא
moves.summary: Abaye substitutes a different source: a baraita expounding the superfluous word עוד.
moves.about: supplies a different source for R' Eliezer's ruling in place of Rabba's split reading

moves.cueHe: ״לֹא יִגָּאֵל״ — יָכוֹל לֹא תְּהֵא נִגְאֶלֶת
moves.summary: The baraita derives from עוד that the field may be redeemed only to the status of a purchased field.
moves.about: the word עוד limits the ban on redemption: it may not be redeemed back to ancestral status but may be redeemed as a purchased field

moves.cueHe: אִילֵּימָא בְּיוֹבֵל רִאשׁוֹן
moves.summary: Floats the first Jubilee cycle as the baraita's case.
moves.about: fixes the baraita as speaking of a redemption during the second Jubilee cycle

moves.cueHe: אַמַּאי אֵינָהּ נִגְאֶלֶת? שְׂדֵה אֲחוּזָּה נָמֵי הָוְיָא!
moves.summary: Knocks that float down: in the first cycle the field is still redeemable as an ancestral field.
moves.about: rejects its own floated reading that the baraita speaks of the first Jubilee cycle, since then the field would still be redeemable as an ancestral field

moves.cueHe: אֶלָּא פְּשִׁיטָא בְּיוֹבֵל שֵׁנִי
moves.summary: Concludes the baraita speaks of the second Jubilee cycle.

moves.cueHe: אֵימַת?
moves.summary: Which Jubilee cycle is the baraita speaking of?
moves.about: which Jubilee cycle the baraita's clause about redemption is speaking of

moves.cueHe: אִילֵימָא לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
moves.summary: Floats R' Yehuda and R' Shimon as the baraita's authors.
moves.about: assigns the anonymous baraita to R' Eliezer, for whom the field stays with the Temple treasury until redeemed

moves.cueHe: לְכֹהֲנִים נָפְקָא!
moves.summary: Rejects them: on their view the field is already the priests' at the first Jubilee and cannot be redeemed.
moves.about: rejects assigning the baraita to R' Yehuda and R' Shimon, for whom the field already passed to the priests at the first Jubilee and can no longer be redeemed

moves.cueHe: אֶלָּא לָאו רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר, וּשְׁמַע מִינַּהּ
moves.summary: Assigns the baraita to R' Eliezer and infers that his reason is the word עוד, supporting Abaye.
moves.about: concludes from the baraita that R' Eliezer's reason is the superfluous word עוד

moves.cueHe: וּלְמַאן?
moves.summary: Whose view does the anonymous baraita follow?
moves.about: which tanna the anonymous baraita follows

moves.cueHe: וְתִסְבְּרָא, רַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן הַאי ״עוֹד״ מַאי דָּרְשִׁי בֵּיהּ?
moves.summary: Refutes that inference: R' Yehuda and R' Shimon would then have nothing to derive from עוד.
moves.about: if the baraita were only R' Eliezer's, what would R' Yehuda and R' Shimon derive from the word עוד

moves.cueHe: אֶלָּא, הָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן — בְּשָׂדֶה שֶׁיָּצְאָה לַכֹּהֲנִים
moves.summary: Re-reads the baraita as a priest's consecration redeemed by the original owner — acceptable to all three tannaim.
moves.about: re-reads the baraita as speaking of a field already given to the priests, consecrated by the priest and now redeemed by its original owner — a reading open to all three tannaim

moves.cueHe: סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ אָמֵינָא: לָא תִּיפְרוֹק
moves.summary: On the new reading, עוד permits the owner to redeem the priest's consecrated field as a purchased field.
moves.about: on the new reading, עוד teaches that the owner may still redeem the priest's consecrated field, though only as a purchased field

moves.cueHe: וְהָתַנְיָא: ״בִּשְׁנַת הַיּוֹבֵל יָשׁוּב הַשָּׂדֶה לַאֲשֶׁר קָנָהוּ מֵאִתּוֹ״
moves.summary: Adds a parallel baraita expounding Leviticus 27:24.
moves.about: adds a parallel baraita on Leviticus 27:24 that reads the same case into a second verse

moves.cueHe: יֵאָמֵר: ״לַאֲשֶׁר לוֹ אֲחֻזַּת הָאָרֶץ״, מָה תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר ״לַאֲשֶׁר קָנָהוּ מֵאִתּוֹ״?
moves.summary: The baraita asks why the extra clause is needed and confines it to a field the priest sold on.
moves.about: confines לאשר קנהו to a field the priest received at the Jubilee and sold on, which the buyer consecrated and a third party redeemed

moves.cueHe: וְאִיצְטְרִיךְ ״לֹא יִגָּאֵל״, וְאִיצְטְרִיכָא לְמִיכְתַּב ״לַאֲשֶׁר קָנָהוּ״
moves.summary: Opens a tzerikhuta: both texts are necessary though they look to teach the same halakha.
moves.about: neither לא יגאל nor לאשר קנהו is redundant, since each covers a case the other would not settle

moves.cueHe: דְּאִי כְּתַב רַחֲמָנָא ״לֹא יִגָּאֵל״
moves.summary: First limb: לא יגאל alone would not have covered a field that does return.
moves.about: לא יגאל alone would have covered only a field that never returns at all, so לאשר קנהו is needed for the field that does return

moves.cueHe: וְאִי כְּתַב רַחֲמָנָא ״לַאֲשֶׁר קָנָהוּ״
moves.summary: Second limb: לאשר קנהו alone would not have covered a case where the owner paid redemption money.
moves.about: לאשר קנהו alone would have covered only where the owner paid nothing, so לא יגאל is needed where he did pay the redemption money

moves.cueHe: וְאִי כְּתַב רַחֲמָנָא ״לֹא יִגָּאֵל״, וְלָא כְּתַב ״עוֹד״
moves.summary: Third limb: without עוד redemption would have been barred entirely.
moves.about: without עוד one would have barred redemption altogether, so עוד is needed to permit redemption as a purchased field

moves.cueHe: מַאי הָוֵי עֲלַהּ?
moves.summary: With both proposals knocked down, asks what R' Eliezer's source actually is.
moves.about: what R' Eliezer's source finally is, now that both Rabba's and Abaye's proposals have been knocked down

moves.cueHe: אָמַר רָבָא, אָמַר קְרָא: ״וְהָיָה הַשָּׂדֶה בְּצֵאתוֹ בַיּוֹבֵל״
moves.summary: Rava settles it: בצאתו means only a field going out of another's possession reaches the priests.
moves.about: settles the standing question of R' Eliezer's scriptural source

moves.cueHe: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: בְּעָלִים בְּיוֹבֵל שֵׁנִי, כְּאַחֵר דָּמוּ אוֹ לָא?
moves.summary: Opens a new dilemma: is an owner who redeems in the second Jubilee cycle the another of R' Eliezer's ruling?
moves.about: whether, for R' Eliezer, an owner who redeems his consecrated ancestral field during the second Jubilee cycle counts as the another whose redemption sends the field to the priests

moves.cueHe: תָּא שְׁמַע: ״לֹא יִגָּאֵל״ — יָכוֹל לֹא תְּהֵא נִגְאֶלֶת
moves.summary: Adduces the עוד baraita as a candidate resolution of the dilemma.
moves.about: brings the עוד baraita again, now against the dilemma about the owner in the second Jubilee cycle

moves.cueHe: אֵימַת? אִילֵּימָא בְּיוֹבֵל רִאשׁוֹן
moves.summary: Floats the first Jubilee cycle as the baraita's case.
moves.about: fixes the baraita as speaking of a redemption during the second Jubilee cycle

moves.cueHe: אַמַּאי אֵינָהּ נִגְאֶלֶת? אֲחוּזָּה נָמֵי הָוְיָא!
moves.summary: Knocks it down and fixes the second Jubilee cycle instead.
moves.about: rejects reading the baraita of the first Jubilee cycle, when the field would still be redeemable as an ancestral field

moves.cueHe: וּלְמַאן? … אֶלָּא לָאו לְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר, וּשְׁמַע מִינַּהּ
moves.summary: Assigns the baraita to R' Eliezer and infers that the owner in the second cycle is like another.
moves.about: concludes from the baraita that for R' Eliezer the owner redeeming in the second Jubilee cycle is like another person

moves.cueHe: וְתִסְבְּרַאּ?! רַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן הַאי ״עוֹד״ מַאי דָּרְשִׁי בֵּיהּ?
moves.summary: Refutes the inference on the same ground as before.
moves.about: attacks its own inference: if the baraita were only R' Eliezer's, R' Yehuda and R' Shimon would have nothing to derive from עוד
